title: Headlines from exclusive FT interview with CEO of ASML Christophe Fouquet
gist: Headlines from an FT interview with ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet: the AI effect will run 10-15 years, over-restricting China could create stronger Chinese competitors, ASML holds a 'total monopoly' on advanced EUV but won't abuse it, and humanoid robots are a few years away.

insights.claim: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet says the AI effect on society and industry will take 10 to 15 years and only the tip of the iceberg is visible.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The key lithography supplier sees a long-duration AI capex cycle, not a near-term peak.
insights.quote: I think the AI effect on society and industry is going to take 10 to 15 years. We’re only seeing the tip of the iceberg.

insights.claim: Fouquet predicts humanoid robots will be among us a few years from now, taking on mundane tasks like gardening and emptying the dishwasher.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Humanoid robotics is being cited by semiconductor leaders as a next demand vector.

insights.claim: Fouquet warns that US pressure to embargo ASML sales to China could backfire: over-restriction creates desperation that accelerates China's own technology and could create strong competitors.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Tighter export controls may cut ASML China revenue near-term while seeding long-term domestic Chinese lithography competition.
insights.quote: If you over-restrict, you bring desperation, and desperation creates a huge appetite for people to accelerate their own technology

insights.claim: ASML has a 'total monopoly' on the most advanced EUV lithography machines essential for producing complex AI chips.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Unique chokepoint position in the AI supply chain underpins ASML's structural moat.
insights.quote: ASML has a “total monopoly” on the most advanced EUV lithography machines
insights.locator: The company at the heart of AI

insights.claim: Fouquet rejects pressure to maximize profits, saying ASML's profit will grow with the industry's but it will not abuse its dominant position.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Signals ASML may leave pricing power on the table, capping margin upside versus a pure monopoly-pricing scenario.
insights.quote: Our profit will grow with the [profits] of the industry, but we are not going to abuse the situation.

insights.claim: Fouquet attributes ASML's success to long-term investment, extreme collaboration and concentration of expertise rather than the Silicon Valley model of aggressive competition and winner-takes-all economics.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Explains ASML's ecosystem-partner posture and long-horizon capital allocation.
